planting.note: Start indoors 6-8 weeks before last frost on the surface of moist mix; transplant into shaded beds or baskets once frost danger has passed.

directions: Unlike the upright bedding torenias sold as Fournieri-type series, this species forms a low mat of trailing stems that root readily as they spread, making it well suited to hanging baskets and as a shaded groundcover under trees. The small, deep violet-blue, two-lipped flowers with a bright yellow throat patch open continuously from midsummer into fall and need no deadheading. Grow in consistently moist, humus-rich soil in part to full shade, since foliage scorches quickly if the plant dries out or receives strong afternoon sun. In zones 8 and warmer it often persists as a short-lived perennial, dying back in hard frost but returning from the base; elsewhere treat as a tender annual.
sources: North Carolina State Extension - Plants Database
